name: Lo Ping-wang
bio: Lo Ping-wang was a poet of the early seventh century, listed in the book among the T'ang poets. His poem here was written in prison, listening to a cicada.
The poem here is Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu's versions in The Jade Mountain (1929), given with the poet's name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: A Political Prisoner Listening to a Cicada
poems.author: Lo Ping-wang
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
While the year sinks westward, I hear a cicada
Bid me to be resolute here in my cell,
Yet it needed the song of those black wings
To break a white-haired prisoner's heart. . . .
His flight is heavy through the fog,
His pure voice drowns in the windy world.
Who knows if he be singing still? —
Who listens any more to me?

poems.title: 易水送別 (Yi shui song bie)
poems.author: Lo Ping-wang
poems.collection: 千家詩 (Poems of a Thousand Poets)
poems.text:
此地別燕丹，壯士發衝冠。
昔時人已沒，今日水猶寒。

poems.title: 詠蟬 (Yong chan)
poems.author: Lo Ping-wang
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.note: 五言律詩. Also titled 在獄詠蟬.
poems.text:
西陸蟬聲唱，南冠客思深。
不堪玄鬢影，來對白頭吟。
露重飛難進，風多響易沉。
無人信高潔，誰爲表予心？
